getting-started.title: Getting started
getting-started.desc: Install claude-multi, add your first provider instance, verify the wrapper, and launch an isolated Claude Code session on macOS, Linux, or Windows.

blocks.html: Applies to claude-multi 0.13.2.
You need two things:

items.html: A JavaScript runtime: Node.js 22+ or Bun 1+

blocks.html: If you don’t have Claude Code yet:
Pick whichever package manager you already use:

blocks.code:
# Bun
bun add -g claude-multi

# npm
npm install -g claude-multi

# pnpm
pnpm add -g claude-multi

blocks.html: The claude-multi launcher is a short shell script. It finds Bun or Node and runs the CLI with the first runtime available. It does not bundle a runtime.
The install commands are the same in PowerShell. Claude Code and claude-multi both need to be on PATH.
The claude-multi launcher is a POSIX shell script, so Windows needs an sh on PATH (Git Bash provides one). The generated claude-<name>.cmd wrappers do not need it.
The generated wrapper is a .cmd file, and its directory depends on the package manager:
If claude-glm is not found after creation, add the directory to your user PATH and open a new terminal:
Replace $env:APPDATA\npm with $env:USERPROFILE\.bun\bin if you installed with Bun.
If wrapper creation cannot find claude, set CLAUDE_MULTI_CLAUDE_PATH to the full path of claude.exe or claude.cmd before you run claude-multi add:
Launch the interactive TUI:
Select Add new instance and follow the wizard:

items.html: Pick a short instance name like glm or deepseek. This becomes your command (claude-glm, claude-deepseek).
Pick a provider template from the list, or choose None / Custom for manual setup.
If you chose the MiMo Token Plan template, pick a region: cn, sgp, or ams.
Paste your API key. The input is masked and the key is stored in the instance’s settings.json.
Accept the default paths: ~/.claude-<name>/ for config, and ~/.local/bin/claude-<name> for the wrapper on macOS and Linux.
Choose what to copy from your default ~/.claude: nothing, settings, selected plugins, or everything.
If you chose to copy plugins or all files, choose a sync mode: auto, half-manual, or full-manual.

blocks.html: Choosing All files copies ~/.claude/settings.json including its env block. If you also picked a provider template, the template replaces the provider keys, but other env entries remain. Review ~/.claude-<name>/settings.json after creation if you do not want the instance to inherit them.
When the wizard finishes:
Run it:
You now have a Claude Code session connected to DeepSeek with its own isolated config. It is the same claude binary, pointed at a different provider.
You can also create instances from the command line instead of the TUI:

blocks.code:
claude-multi add deepseek --provider deepseek --api-key sk-your-key --skip-prompts
claude-multi add glm --provider glm --api-key your-zai-key --skip-prompts

blocks.html: --provider requires --api-key. Without the key, the command exits with an error instead of prompting.
Run the instances:
List the instances:
Expected output for one instance:

blocks.code:
Found 1 instance(s):

● glm
  Binary:  /Users/you/.local/bin/claude-glm
  Config:  /Users/you/.claude-glm
  Created: 10/31/2026, 10:00:00 AM
  Provider: glm
  Sync mode: Auto-sync (symlink dirs)
  Version:  0.13.2

blocks.html: The date format follows your locale. Then check that the wrapper reaches Claude Code:
The output is Claude Code’s version, in the form 2.x.x (Claude Code). claude-multi does not change that number. To check the claude-multi version itself:
It prints 0.13.2 on this release.
On macOS and Linux, if claude-<name> isn’t found after creation, your global binary directory probably isn’t on PATH. Add it once:

blocks.code:
# zsh (macOS default)
echo 'export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.zshrc
source ~/.zshrc

# bash
echo 'export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.bashrc
source ~/.bashrc

blocks.html: The wrapper defaults to ~/.local/bin/claude-<name> on macOS and Linux. The creation output and claude-multi list print the actual path, including a custom --binary value.
Remove one instance:
This removes the registry entry and deletes the wrapper. It leaves ~/.claude-glm/ on disk and prints the path. Delete it yourself when you no longer need its history or settings:
On Windows:
Remove the package with the same manager you used to install it:

blocks.code:
# npm
npm uninstall -g claude-multi

# Bun
bun remove -g claude-multi

# pnpm
pnpm remove -g claude-multi

blocks.html: After removing every instance, you can delete the central state:
That directory holds the registry, health status, and up to three migration backup sets. Deleting it does not touch ~/.claude or any ~/.claude-<name>/ directory.
To roll back to an earlier claude-multi release, install a specific version:

blocks.code:
npm view claude-multi versions
npm install -g claude-multi@<version>

blocks.html: Downgrading the CLI does not downgrade instance config. Back up ~/.claude-multi/ and the affected ~/.claude-<name>/settings.json files before you try. Migration backups live in ~/.claude-multi/backups/, and claude-multi keeps the newest three.

usage.title: Usage
usage.desc: CLI command reference for claude-multi 0.13.2: add, remove, list, sync, doctor, plugins, and MCP commands.

blocks.html: Running claude-multi with no arguments launches the interactive terminal UI. Most CLI actions also live in the menu.
Use arrow keys to navigate, Enter to select, ESC to go back, q to quit. If the Ink-based TUI doesn’t render on your terminal, force the simpler prompts UI:

head: Flag
Description
rows: API key for the provider. Required when --provider is used
Region for mimo-token: cn, sgp, or ams. Defaults to cn with a warning
Custom wrapper path (default: ~/.local/bin/claude-<name> on macOS and Linux, package manager bin on Windows)
Copy the default config directory, including settings.json, CLAUDE.md, and plugins. History and session state are excluded
Skip interactive prompts and start fresh
Set sync mode at creation: auto, half-manual, or full-manual

blocks.html: Use only one sync flag per command. Passing more than one exits with an error before anything is written. Sync flags apply to the scripted path. If you run add without --provider, --skip-prompts, or a copy flag, claude-multi opens the wizard. The wizard asks for the sync mode when you choose to copy plugins or all files.
Examples:

blocks.code:
# Interactive: the TUI asks for provider, key, paths, and copy options
claude-multi add deepseek

# Non-interactive, fully scripted
claude-multi add deepseek --provider deepseek --api-key sk-your-key --skip-prompts

# MiMo Token Plan in Singapore
claude-multi add mimo-sg --provider mimo-token --api-key tp_your-key --region sgp --skip-prompts

# Start from your default setup, then apply the GLM template
claude-multi add glm --provider glm --api-key your-zai-key --copy-all --skip-prompts

blocks.html: --provider without --api-key is an error. The CLI does not fall back to a prompt in that form. Use claude-multi add glm with no flags if you want to be asked for the key.
--copy-all requires an existing ~/.claude directory. If it is missing, the command removes the partially created instance and wrapper, then exits with an error.
Alias: claude-multi rm <name>.
This removes the instance from the registry and deletes the wrapper script. It leaves the config directory on disk and prints the rm -rf command for it.
Alias: claude-multi ls.
Shows every instance with its wrapper path, config path, creation date, provider and region, sync mode, and the claude-multi version it was created with.
Displays the same fields for one instance without the surrounding list.

blocks.code:
# Check the installed Claude Code version and whether an update is available
claude-multi version

# Update @anthropic-ai/claude-code
claude-multi update

blocks.html: These commands manage the @anthropic-ai/claude-code package, not claude-multi. To update claude-multi itself, use your package manager (npm update -g claude-multi, bun update -g claude-multi, and so on). claude-multi --version prints the claude-multi version.
Plugin and skill syncing has three modes. Set one at creation or change it later:

blocks.code:
# At creation, in a scripted add
claude-multi add <name> --provider deepseek --api-key sk-... --sync-mode half-manual --skip-prompts

# Later
claude-multi auto-sync <name> <auto|half-manual|full-manual>

blocks.html: Legacy on/off still work with auto-sync (on maps to auto, off maps to full-manual).

head: Mode
Behavior
rows: plugins/ and skills/ are symlinked whole to ~/.claude/. Any change there is instantly visible to the instance.
Real directories, but each plugin and skill inside is individually symlinked back to ~/.claude/. You keep the existing plugins, but new installs in ~/.claude don’t appear until you re-sync.
Independent copies of everything. No symlinks. The instance can drift freely from ~/.claude.

blocks.html: Conversions are one-way: auto to half-manual to full-manual. claude-multi rejects upgrades because reconciling directories that have diverged is a data-loss problem. The TUI Sync Mode screen shows the current mode and which downgrades are available, plus a Force re-sync option that rebuilds symlinks without changing the mode.
In auto and half-manual modes, plugins install and plugins remove are blocked. Both operate on real files, and both modes use symlinks. Switch to full-manual first.
If symlinks break because you moved or deleted ~/.claude, repair them with claude-multi fix-symlinks.

Without names, claude-multi asks which instances to repair. The command rebuilds whole-directory symlinks in auto mode and per-item symlinks in half-manual mode. It reports full-manual instances as having no symlinks to repair.

blocks.code:
claude-multi doctor check
claude-multi doctor fix

blocks.html: doctor check runs the health checks and prints each issue with a suggested fix. It reports missing config directories, missing wrappers, invalid settings.json files, broken symlinks, wrappers that point at a different claude binary, region URL mismatches, and pending instance migrations. Pending migrations include provider settings that differ from the current template.

doctor fix does two things. It rewrites wrappers that point at a stale Claude binary, then asks whether to run pending instance migrations. Migrations create a backup, refresh provider env from the current template, and record the migration version. API keys and custom tunable values survive, except for documented legacy defaults that the migration replaces.
The TUI shows Run instance migrations when the same work is pending.
All plugin commands use the plugins subcommand:

head: Action
Description
rows: List enabled plugins. With no instance, shows the default setup and every instance
Enable one or more plugins for an instance. Use the full plugin-id@marketplace-name key
Copy plugins from ~/.claude into the instance. Full-manual only
Copy the enabled plugin map from ~/.claude/settings.json into one instance
List plugins available in ~/.claude, with category and MCP badges
List plugin files installed in one instance, or in every instance
Check whether the named plugins register MCP server names already in use

blocks.html: plugins copy takes one instance name. It reads enabledPlugins from ~/.claude/settings.json and writes that map into the instance’s settings.json. It does not copy plugin files. Use plugins install for files, or plugins copy for the enable/disable list.

Claude Code stores plugin keys as plugin-id@marketplace-name. enable and disable take that full key, while install and remove take the bare plugin ID. Plugins from the official marketplace use @claude-plugins-official.
plugins install refuses to run while a Claude Code session is open on that instance. Close the session first.
plugins remove stages the plugin directory under a temporary .removing name, deletes it, and restores it if the delete fails.

head: Action
Description
rows: List MCP server configs. With no instance, shows every instance
Copy MCP server configs between instances, with prompts for source and target
Check that each server entry has the fields its transport needs

blocks.html: Run claude-multi mcp copy with no extra arguments and answer the prompts. The command replaces the target instance’s mcpServers block with the source instance’s block. It does not merge them.

mcp verify checks config shape, not whether a server process starts. It confirms that stdio entries have a command and that HTTP and SSE entries have a url. Use /mcp inside a session to check the live connection.

head: Variable
Default
Description
rows: Set to false to use the simpler prompts-based UI instead of Ink
Base directory for central state such as migration backups and health status
Absolute path to the claude binary. Overrides the PATH lookup when wrappers are created or repaired
Set to true to check for updates on launch

blocks.html: See Environment variables for the full reference, including the keys provider templates write into settings.json.
Each instance is an independent command, so switching means running a different one. You do not edit config or export environment variables.

blocks.code:
claude-glm "explain this function"
claude-deepseek "write tests for auth.ts"

blocks.html: Both are simultaneous Claude Code sessions. Open two terminals and they don’t interfere with each other.
Most day-to-day work like renaming variables or updating docs does not need a frontier model. Keep a cheap instance for routine tasks and a stronger one for hard problems:

blocks.code:
claude-multi add budget --provider deepseek --api-key sk-... --skip-prompts
claude-multi add power --provider glm --api-key your-key --skip-prompts

claude-budget "add error handling to all fetch calls"   # routine
claude-power "redesign the auth module to support SAML" # needs judgment

blocks.html: Auto-sync both if you want them to share plugins and skills with ~/.claude. MCP servers stay per-instance in each settings.json; auto-sync does not copy them.
Marketing pages claim every model is the best. Test against your own code instead. Create one instance per provider, run the same prompt through each, and compare the results.

blocks.code:
claude-multi add test-glm --provider glm --api-key ... --skip-prompts
claude-multi add test-deepseek --provider deepseek --api-key ... --skip-prompts

claude-test-glm -p "find the memory leak in src/cache.ts"
claude-test-deepseek -p "find the memory leak in src/cache.ts"

blocks.html: Remove the test instances once you have picked a winner, or keep them for a periodic re-check.
Mixing contexts in one config leaks your work API key into personal sessions and tangles the conversation history. Give each context its own instance:

blocks.code:
claude-multi add work --provider glm --api-key work-key --skip-prompts
claude-multi add personal --provider deepseek --api-key personal-key --skip-prompts

blocks.html: Set both to full-manual if you want separate plugins and skills too. Two auto instances still share ~/.claude/plugins and ~/.claude/skills.

blocks.code:
claude-multi auto-sync work full-manual
claude-multi auto-sync personal full-manual

blocks.html: Create one reference instance with your team’s provider, plugins, MCP servers, and CLAUDE.md, then have each new hire recreate it from their own ~/.claude:

--copy-all copies settings, CLAUDE.md, plugins, and skills from ~/.claude. It also copies the default settings.json, including its env block. Review ~/.claude-team/settings.json after creation and remove keys you do not want to carry over. The provider template replaces the provider env keys with the values for the key passed on the command line. Store the non-secret parts of the setup in your dotfiles repo and let each person supply their own key.
Reviewed 2026-11-03

how-it-works.title: How it works
how-it-works.desc: How claude-multi isolates Claude Code instances with config directories, environment variables, plugin symlinks, and wrapper scripts.

blocks.html: claude-multi doesn’t fork, patch, or modify Claude Code. Each instance is a small script that does two things: set CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, then exec the real claude binary.
On Windows, the same thing in batch:

That is the entire mechanism. Claude Code reads its config from the directory you point it at instead of ~/.claude. Everything else behaves normally: flags, commands, keybindings, plugins, and MCP servers.
The wrapper records the resolved claude path at creation time. If you move or reinstall Claude Code, run claude-multi doctor fix to rewrite wrappers that still point at the old path.

blocks.code:
~/.claude-multi/
├── config.json              # instance registry
├── health-status.json       # persistent health issue tracking
├── backups/                 # migration backups (newest 3 kept)
└── .migration.lock          # PID-based migration lock

~/.claude-deepseek/          # one instance
├── settings.json            # provider env, enabled plugins, MCP servers
├── .claude.json             # Claude Code state (onboarding, user ID, migration version)
├── plugins/                 # symlinked, half-symlinked, or copied
├── skills/                  # symlinked, half-symlinked, or copied
└── projects/                # conversation history per project

~/.local/bin/
└── claude-deepseek          # wrapper script

head: Path
Purpose
rows: Central registry: instance names, config paths, wrapper paths, creation dates, sync modes, created-with versions, provider templates, and regions
Health issues and their dismissed or resolved state
Migration backups, up to three sets
PID-based lock so two migrations cannot run at once
Per-instance config directory. Mirrors Claude Code’s ~/.claude structure
Onboarding state, user ID, and Claude Code migration version
Generated wrapper on macOS and Linux

blocks.html: On Windows, the wrapper is claude-<name>.cmd and lives in the package manager’s global bin directory: %APPDATA%\npm for npm and pnpm, or %USERPROFILE%\.bun\bin for Bun.

Each instance is independent. It has its own settings.json holding provider env vars, enabled plugins, and MCP servers. It has its own .claude.json holding onboarding state, migration version, and user ID. Its plugins/ and skills/ directories are symlinked back to ~/.claude in auto mode, per-item symlinked in half-manual mode, or kept as separate copies in full-manual mode. Its projects/ directory holds a conversation history that no other instance can see.
Two instances can run at the same time in different terminals. They share no state, take no lock files, and bind no ports.

Sync has three modes: auto, half-manual, and full-manual. In auto mode, an instance’s plugins/ and skills/ are symlinked to ~/.claude/, so a change there is immediately visible to every synced instance. The other modes trade that immediacy for per-instance control.

Only plugins/ and skills/ are symlinked. MCP servers are entries in each instance’s settings.json and stay with that instance. A plugin can still carry its own MCP server in a .mcp.json file, and that server arrives with the plugin directory when the plugin is symlinked.
See Sync modes for the full comparison and Plugins and MCP for the operational detail, including claude-multi fix-symlinks for broken links.

A provider template is a bundle of environment variables (base URL, model slots, thinking settings, output limits) and a few Claude Code settings. claude-multi merges the template into an instance’s settings.json when it creates the instance. You supply the API key.
This is what the deepseek template writes into settings.json in 0.13.2, with the key filled in:
Templates are plain config. They install nothing and make no network calls. The only thing they change about Claude Code is the endpoint it talks to and the model names it sends.

Qwen coverage differs by plan. The pay-per-token qwen template maps Qwen3.8-Max, Qwen3.7-Plus, and Qwen3.8-Flash. The qwen-coding template uses Qwen3.7-Plus in every slot because the Coding Plan does not include Qwen3.8-Max or Qwen3.8-Flash. Environment variables has the full mapping.
Creating an instance copies the current provider template into its settings.json. claude-multi does not apply later template updates in the background.
After upgrading claude-multi, run:

blocks.code:
claude-multi doctor check
claude-multi doctor fix

blocks.html: doctor check reports health issues, including pending instance migrations. Pending migrations cover instances created by an older claude-multi version and provider settings that differ from the current template. doctor fix rewrites wrappers that point at the wrong Claude binary, then asks whether to run the migrations. A migration backs up the affected config.json and settings.json files first.
The fix restores provider model slots and other template settings. It leaves your API keys and custom tuning values alone, except for known legacy defaults that have to change with the template.
See Providers for the full template reference.
The two copy paths behave differently.
--copy-settings and the TUI’s Only settings.json option transfer only three fields. The TUI’s Select plugins to install option uses the same settings copy, then adds the plugins you pick:
They never copy the env block, which holds API keys.

--copy-all and the TUI’s All files option copy settings.json as a file. That includes its env block. If you use --copy-all together with --provider, the provider template merges its own env over the copied values, but unrelated keys from the default file remain. Open ~/.claude-<name>/settings.json and remove any key you do not want the instance to inherit.
claude-multi runs health checks across all instances. It looks for:

items.html: Wrappers that point at a different claude binary
Region URL mismatches on regional templates

blocks.html: If it finds anything, the TUI shows a warning banner. Press ! to open the health screen, which lists each problem and its suggested fix.
When the config format changes between versions, claude-multi migrates it for you:

items.html: Creates a timestamped backup directory under ~/.claude-multi/backups/ containing config.json and each instance’s settings.json
Saves atomically with a temp-file rename

blocks.html: Migrations take a PID-based lock so two cannot run at once. A failed migration sets migrationMeta.migrationStatus to failed and records the error. The health screen shows the failure detail. If the config is unusable, restore the newest backup directory. claude-multi keeps the newest three.

The claude-multi binary in bin/claude-multi.js is a short POSIX shell script, not JavaScript. It resolves symlinks, locates build/cli.js, and execs the first runtime it finds: Bun, then Node. If none is installed, it prints an error and exits.
The generated instance wrappers are separate. They are /bin/sh scripts on macOS and Linux and .cmd batch files on Windows. They need no JavaScript runtime at launch.
Reviewed 2026-11-03

plugins-mcp.title: Plugins and MCP
plugins-mcp.desc: Install plugins and configure MCP servers across claude-multi instances, with sync modes, collision checks, and verification steps.

blocks.html: Plugins and MCP servers are different things, and claude-multi handles them differently.

A plugin is a directory of skills, commands, agents, hooks, or MCP server definitions. It lives under the instance’s plugins/ directory. Depending on the sync mode, that directory is a symlink to ~/.claude/plugins, a directory of per-item symlinks, or a real copy.

An MCP server is a single entry in the instance’s settings.json under mcpServers. It describes how Claude Code starts or connects to a server: a command and args for stdio, or a URL for HTTP and SSE. claude-multi does not symlink individual MCP entries. It edits the settings file.
A plugin can carry its own MCP server in a .mcp.json file. That server arrives with the plugin. Servers you add yourself live only in the instance whose settings file you edited.
Internal plugins live under plugins/marketplaces/claude-plugins-official/plugins/. External plugins live under external_plugins/ in the same marketplace directory.

blocks.code:
~/.claude-deepseek/plugins/
├── installed_plugins.json
└── marketplaces/
    └── claude-plugins-official/
        ├── known_marketplaces.json
        ├── blocklist.json
        ├── plugins/
        │   └── some-plugin/
        │       ├── .claude-plugin/plugin.json
        │       └── .mcp.json
        └── external_plugins/
            └── another-plugin/
                ├── .claude-plugin/plugin.json
                └── .mcp.json

blocks.html: installed_plugins.json is the v2 tracking file. It maps a plugin key to an array of install records with scope, install path, version, and timestamps.
From the TUI, select Manage plugins, pick an instance, and choose List installed plugins.
From the CLI:

blocks.code:
# List plugins available in ~/.claude, with category and MCP badges
claude-multi plugins list-defaults

# List installed plugins for one instance
claude-multi plugins list-installed deepseek

# List enabled plugins for one instance
claude-multi plugins list deepseek

blocks.html: plugins list with no instance shows the default setup and every instance. plugins list-installed with no instance shows every instance.
plugins install copies plugin files from ~/.claude into one instance. It works only in full-manual mode, because auto and half-manual use symlinks.
From the TUI, select Manage plugins, pick an instance, then Install plugins from default. Use space to toggle plugins and enter to confirm.
From the CLI:

Before copying, claude-multi checks whether the plugin would register an MCP server name that another installed plugin already uses. If it finds a collision, it prints a warning and then continues. Run check-collisions first if you want to stop before writing.
plugins install refuses to run while a Claude Code session is open on the target instance.
These commands change the plugin map in settings.json. They do not move files.

blocks.code:
claude-multi plugins enable deepseek some-plugin@claude-plugins-official
claude-multi plugins disable deepseek some-plugin@claude-plugins-official

blocks.html: Claude Code stores plugin keys in plugin-id@marketplace-name form. Plugins from the official marketplace use @claude-plugins-official. Pass the full key to enable and disable; install and remove take the bare plugin ID.
plugins copy takes one instance name. It reads enabledPlugins from ~/.claude/settings.json and writes that map into the instance’s settings.json.
It does not copy plugin files, and there is no instance-to-instance form. Use plugins install for files, or edit the two settings files directly if you need a different mapping.

Removal works only in full-manual mode. claude-multi renames the plugin directory to a temporary .removing path, deletes it, and restores it if the delete fails. It also removes the plugin from installed_plugins.json.

This checks whether the named plugins register an MCP server name that is already used by an installed plugin. It compares names, not server contents. The command exits with status 1 when it finds a collision.
Sync has three modes, which control how an instance’s plugins/ and skills/ relate to ~/.claude/:

head: Mode
What the instance gets
rows: Whole-directory symlinks to ~/.claude/plugins and ~/.claude/skills. Install and remove are blocked.
Real directories with per-item symlinks to each plugin and skill. New installs in ~/.claude do not appear until a re-sync. Install and remove are blocked.
Independent copies with no symlinks. Per-plugin operations work.

blocks.html: Conversions are one-way: auto to half-manual to full-manual. claude-multi rejects upgrades because reconciling directories that have diverged is a data-loss problem.
Legacy on and off still work (on maps to auto, off maps to full-manual). See Sync modes for the full command reference.
If you move or delete ~/.claude, symlinks across every synced instance break. Rebuild them with:
From the TUI, Re-sync symlinks does the same thing.

blocks.text: End-to-end: install a plugin and verify it

blocks.html: This example installs a plugin into a deepseek instance running in full-manual mode.
Find the plugin ID.
Switch the instance to full-manual if it is still synced. Skip this if claude-multi info deepseek already shows full-manual.
Install the plugin.
Enable it.
Verify the files and tracking entry.
The plugin should appear with a checkmark and an [ext] badge when it came from external_plugins/. You can also inspect ~/.claude-deepseek/plugins/installed_plugins.json.
Start the instance and use the plugin’s skill or command.
Plugin skills and commands load from the instance’s own plugins/ directory. If the plugin ships an MCP server, run /mcp to confirm the server connected.
From the TUI, select MCP servers, then List MCP servers with sources.
From the CLI:

blocks.code:
# Every instance
claude-multi mcp list

# One instance
claude-multi mcp list deepseek

blocks.html: The output shows each server’s transport type and, for stdio servers, the command and args. For HTTP and SSE servers it shows the URL.
The command prompts for a source and a target. It replaces the target’s mcpServers block with the source’s block. It does not merge the two.
From the TUI, select MCP servers, then Copy between instances.
This checks config shape. A stdio entry needs a command; an HTTP or SSE entry needs a url. It does not start the server or test the connection. Use /mcp inside a session for that.
From the TUI, select MCP servers, pick an instance, then Add custom MCP server. Enter a name and the JSON config.
From the CLI or an editor, add the entry to ~/.claude-<name>/settings.json:
MCP servers load when a Claude Code session starts. Save the file, then restart the instance.

blocks.text: End-to-end: add a server and check it

items.html: Add the server entry to ~/.claude-deepseek/settings.json as shown above, or use Add custom MCP server in the TUI.

blocks.html: Check that the entry has the fields its transport needs.
Restart the instance.

items.html: Run /mcp inside the session. It lists connected servers and their tools.

blocks.html: If the server is missing from /mcp, the problem is usually the command path, a missing executable, or a port that is not listening. mcp verify will not catch those because it only reads the config.

Some servers should reach only specific instances. A production database server has no business being reachable from a sandbox instance. Configure it in that instance’s settings.json only. Sync mode does not change this, since MCP entries are never symlinked.

head: Problem
Fix
rows: Check the command path in settings.json and confirm the command runs in your shell
Verify the server is running and the port is correct
Check the server’s own logs for startup errors
Switch the instance to full-manual and close any open session

blocks.html: See Troubleshooting for PATH, auth, and migration issues. See Configuration for the full settings.json layout.

configuration.title: Configuration
configuration.desc: Configuration reference for claude-multi 0.13.2: the instance registry, settings.json, .claude.json, plugin tracking, health status, and migration backups.

blocks.html: claude-multi tracks all instances in a central registry at ~/.claude-multi/config.json. The file holds names and paths, not API keys.

head: Field
Type
Description
rows: Last claude-multi version whose instance migrations ran
Present after a schema migration runs
ISO 8601 timestamp of the last migration attempt
Failed step, error message, timestamp, and whether a retry is possible

head: Field
Type
Description
rows: Instance name. Letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores
Absolute path to the instance’s config directory
Absolute path to the generated wrapper
Deprecated. false maps to full-manual; any other value falls back to auto
claude-multi version that created the instance. Instances from before version tracking show 0.5
Optional template name, such as glm or mimo-token

blocks.html: If syncMode is missing, claude-multi reads autoSync for backward compatibility. autoSync: false resolves to full-manual. Everything else resolves to auto.
Each instance has its own settings.json at ~/.claude-<name>/settings.json. This is the same format Claude Code uses natively.

env holds the environment variables Claude Code receives when it launches for this instance. Provider templates fill the provider-specific keys, and each instance’s file has its own ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN entry. Environment variables documents every key and the values each template ships with.

Map of plugin keys to enabled or disabled state. Claude Code uses the plugin-id@marketplace-name form. The map lists the plugins with an explicit state, whether you toggled them by hand or copied them from ~/.claude.
Map of MCP server names to their configuration. The type field accepts stdio, http, and sse.
MCP entries are not symlinked. They stay in the instance’s own settings file regardless of sync mode. See Plugins and MCP for the management commands.
Each instance has a .claude.json at ~/.claude-<name>/.claude.json. claude-multi writes it during setup so Claude Code skips its first-run wizard.

blocks.code:
{
  "numStartups": 1,
  "installMethod": "global",
  "autoUpdates": true,
  "hasSeenTasksHint": true,
  "hasCompletedOnboarding": true,
  "lastOnboardingVersion": "2.0.31",
  "firstStartTime": "2026-10-31T10:00:00.000Z",
  "userID": "64-character-hex-string",
  "promptQueueUseCount": 0,
  "sonnet45MigrationComplete": true,
  "opus45MigrationComplete": true,
  "thinkingMigrationComplete": true,
  "sonnet1m45MigrationComplete": true,
  "opusProMigrationComplete": true,
  "migrationVersion": 13
}

blocks.html: hasCompletedOnboarding: true skips the first-run wizard. userID is 32 random bytes encoded as hex. Claude Code adds other fields as you use the instance, so treat this file as Claude Code state rather than a claude-multi config file.
claude-multi tracks installed plugins in ~/.claude-<name>/plugins/installed_plugins.json. The file uses v2 format, where each plugin key maps to an array of install records.

installPath points at the marketplace directory, not the individual plugin directory. The plugin files themselves live under plugins/marketplaces/claude-plugins-official/plugins/<plugin-id>/ or external_plugins/<plugin-id>/.
Health issues are stored at ~/.claude-multi/health-status.json:

blocks.code:
{
  "lastChecked": "2026-10-31T10:00:00.000Z",
  "issues": [
    {
      "id": "broken-symlinks-deepseek",
      "severity": "warning",
      "category": "symlink",
      "title": "Broken symlinks",
      "message": "Instance 'deepseek' has broken symlinks: plugins",
      "detail": "plugins",
      "instanceName": "deepseek",
      "timestamp": "2026-10-31T10:00:00.000Z",
      "dismissed": false,
      "resolved": false,
      "resolutionHint": "Re-sync symlinks from the home screen"
    }
  ]
}

blocks.html: Severity is error, warning, or info. You can dismiss issues from the TUI health screen. claude-multi finds them again on the next check if the problem is still there.
When the config format changes or an instance migration runs, claude-multi creates a timestamped backup directory:

blocks.code:
~/.claude-multi/backups/
└── 2026-10-31T10-00-00-000Z-a1b2-v2.0.0-to-v2.0.0/
    ├── config.json
    └── instances/
        ├── deepseek/
        │   └── settings.json
        └── glm/
            └── settings.json

blocks.html: The directory name includes the timestamp, a short random suffix, and the source and target config versions. Each backup contains the registry and every instance’s settings.json. claude-multi keeps the newest three backup directories and deletes older ones.

head: Path
Purpose
rows: Per-instance env, plugins, and MCP servers
Wrapper script on macOS and Linux

environment-variables.title: Environment variables
environment-variables.desc: Runtime variables for claude-multi and the Claude Code env keys that provider templates write into each instance's settings.json.

blocks.html: These control claude-multi itself. Set them in your shell before launching.

head: Variable
Default
Description
rows: Set to false to use the simpler prompts-based UI instead of the Ink TUI
Base directory for central state. Health status and migration backups resolve under $CLAUDE_MULTI_HOME/.claude-multi/
Absolute path to the claude binary. Overrides the PATH lookup when wrappers are created or repaired. The file must exist
Set to true to check for claude-multi and Claude Code updates on launch

blocks.html: Examples:

blocks.code:
# Use the simpler UI
CLAUDE_MULTI_INK=false claude-multi

# Point wrapper creation at a specific Claude Code install
CLAUDE_MULTI_CLAUDE_PATH=/opt/claude/bin/claude claude-multi add glm

# Store central state under a test directory
CLAUDE_MULTI_HOME=/tmp/test-env claude-multi doctor check

blocks.html: CLAUDE_MULTI_HOME does not move an instance’s config directory. Each instance still lives at ~/.claude-<name>/ unless you pass --config to add. The instance registry still resolves from your home directory, so this variable is mainly useful for tests and isolated health or migration runs.
These live in each instance’s settings.json under the env key. Provider templates fill them in. You can edit them by hand or let claude-multi doctor fix refresh them from the current template.

head: Variable
Description
Example
rows: Bearer token for the Authorization header. Provider API keys go here

head: Variable
Description
Maps to
rows: Deprecated. Use ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL for the fast model
Superseded by ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL; current templates do not write it
Used when Claude Code requests a “sonnet” class model
Used when Claude Code requests an “opus” class model
Used by the fable alias and automatic fallback. Without it, Claude Code asks the provider for claude-fable-5-1, which a third-party endpoint cannot serve
Used when Claude Code requests a “haiku” class model, and by most templates for the fast slot

head: Variable
Description
Example
rows: Default model for subagents, agent teams, and workflow agents. A per-invocation model or an agent definition’s model field can override it
Reasoning effort for the main model. Accepted values depend on the model
Set to 1 to send the effort parameter for custom model IDs. Templates that set an effort level include it because Claude Code cannot infer effort support from a third-party model name
Fixed thinking budget in tokens. Applies only to models that accept a budget; adaptive-reasoning models and providers that use an effort parameter can ignore it

blocks.html: Claude Code caps output at 128,000 tokens for an unrecognized model ID and defaults to 32,000 when the variable is unset. A model that lists a larger maximum output cannot exceed the Claude Code cap.

head: Variable
Description
Example
rows: Time in milliseconds each request attempt has to receive response headers. It does not cap how long a streaming response runs
Disables nonessential traffic. The GLM and MiniMax templates set it to 1

blocks.html: Claude Code assumes a 200K context window for an unrecognized model ID. When the real window differs, tell Claude Code with the [1m] suffix on the model name or with CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS. Without that, compaction runs against the wrong window and the API call can fail mid-session.

Claude Code compresses older conversation history once usage crosses a share of the window. CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW sets the window used for that decision; it accepts values from 100,000 to 1,000,000. CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE sets the percentage that triggers compaction.

head: Variable
Description
Example
rows: Context window override. Applies directly to unrecognized non-claude- IDs without [1m]; with [1m], pair it with CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_1M_CONTEXT=1; for recognized IDs it needs DISABLE_COMPACT
Window used to decide when to compact, in tokens. Range is 100000 to 1000000
Percentage of the window that triggers compaction. It can only make compaction happen earlier; values above the default are ignored

blocks.html: The templates set this window at or below the model’s context limit. Values below 100,000 or above 1,000,000 are outside the supported range.
Each template writes its own base URL, model slots, timeout, and tuning values. This table matches src/templates.ts in 0.13.2.

The primary column shows ANTHROPIC_MODEL. The Fable column shows ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_FABLE_MODEL. The fast column shows ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL. Templates that set CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL point it at the fast model.
Every template maps the fable alias to its primary model. Claude Code otherwise resolves fable to claude-fable-5-1, and a third-party Anthropic-compatible endpoint rejects that ID.
Other defaults that differ by template:

The mimo-token base URL depends on the region you picked at creation. cn uses token-plan-cn.xiaomimimo.com, sgp uses token-plan-sgp.xiaomimimo.com, and ams uses token-plan-ams.xiaomimimo.com. All three keep the /anthropic path.
The 0.13.2 templates match the current vendor model lists as of 2026-11-03. The notes below cover plan coverage and model availability where they affect a slot.

The qwen template maps qwen3.8-max to the primary, opus, and fable slots, qwen3.7-plus to sonnet, and qwen3.8-flash to haiku and subagents. It sets CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS=983616 and compacts at 75 percent. It does not set an effort level, so the provider default applies.

The qwen-coding template uses qwen3.7-plus in every slot. The Coding Plan includes Qwen3.7-Plus but not Qwen3.8-Max or Qwen3.8-Flash. That is a plan limit, not an endpoint limit. If the plan rejects requests above 200K, lower CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS to 200000.
qwen3-coder-next and qwen3-coder-plus are absent from the current Anthropic-compatible model matrix. Only qwen3-coder-flash remains as a legacy Coder model.

The minimax template uses MiniMax-M3.1-Flash[1m] in every slot, including Fable and subagents, with a 524288 auto-compact window. It sets effort to max and adds CLAUDE_CODE_ALWAYS_ENABLE_EFFORT=1. M3 is the previous generation and remains available. MiniMax says a Pro model will follow, but no ID or date is published.

The deepseek template uses deepseek-flash[1m] for primary, opus, sonnet, and Fable, and deepseek-flash for haiku and subagents, with a 786432 auto-compact window. It sets effort to max and adds CLAUDE_CODE_ALWAYS_ENABLE_EFFORT=1. deepseek-flash serves V4.1-Flash-1017. deepseek-v4-pro is V4-Pro-0813, the previous generation, and remains available as an optional model. There is no released V4.1 Pro.
DeepSeek’s Anthropic endpoint ignores budget_tokens, so MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=32000 is a client-side hint, not a provider budget. Thinking depth follows CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL.

The mimo and mimo-token templates use mimo-v2.6-pro[1m] for primary, opus, sonnet, and Fable, and mimo-v2.6-flash[1m] for haiku and subagents. Both models have a 1M context window and 128K output. The templates do not set an effort level. See Xiaomi MiMo for setup details.

The kimi template uses kimi-k3.1-pro[1m] in every slot, including Fable. Standard speed is the default. Highspeed is optional and costs more per token. It sets effort to max and adds CLAUDE_CODE_ALWAYS_ENABLE_EFFORT=1. Kimi always thinks and has no thinking-budget parameter, so MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=16000 is only a client hint. See Moonshot Kimi for setup details.

The glm template maps glm-5.3[1m] to the primary, opus, sonnet, and Fable slots and glm-5.3-flash[1m] to haiku. It sets effort to high and adds CLAUDE_CODE_ALWAYS_ENABLE_EFFORT=1. Z.ai’s current default configuration maps opus, sonnet, and haiku to glm-5.3-flash[1m]; the template keeps the manual split so the main slots use the flagship model. GLM-5-Turbo is not a Coding Plan model and is not a template tier.

If you created an instance before 0.13.2 (including 0.13.0 and 0.13.1), run claude-multi doctor check, then claude-multi doctor fix. The sync updates model slots, the Fable alias, the effort opt-in, and known legacy defaults while keeping your API key and custom values.
claude-multi variables go in your shell profile (.zshrc, .bashrc, .profile) or in the environment before you run claude-multi.

Instance variables go in ~/.claude-<name>/settings.json under env. The provider template fills them when you create the instance, and they apply to that instance only. They do not affect other instances or your default ~/.claude setup. See Configuration for the file layout and Plugins and MCP for MCP server settings.
Reviewed 2026-11-03

troubleshooting.title: Troubleshooting
troubleshooting.desc: Fix common claude-multi issues: command not found, auth errors, broken plugin symlinks, MCP servers that will not load, and failed migrations.

blocks.html: Your global binary directory is not on PATH, or the wrapper is missing.
The wrapper directory depends on the platform and, on Windows, the package manager:
A custom --binary path overrides these defaults.
Add the directory printed by claude-multi list to your PATH. For a quick test in the current shell:
For persistent setup on zsh, bash, and PowerShell, see Getting started. claude-multi add also prints a warning when the wrapper directory is not on PATH.
If the directory is already on PATH but the command still fails, check whether the wrapper exists and points at the right binary:

blocks.code:
claude-multi doctor check
claude-multi doctor fix

blocks.html: doctor check reports a missing wrapper or a wrapper that points at a different claude binary. doctor fix rewrites wrappers that exist but point at the wrong binary. It does not recreate a wrapper you deleted. In that case, remove the instance and create it again with the same name.
If you moved or deleted ~/.claude/, the symlinks in auto-synced and half-synced instances point at nothing.
From the TUI, select Re-sync symlinks and pick the broken instance or all instances.
From the CLI:

blocks.code:
# Fix a specific instance
claude-multi fix-symlinks deepseek

# Fix all instances
claude-multi fix-symlinks --all

blocks.html: fix-symlinks rebuilds whole-directory links in auto mode and per-item links in half-manual mode. Full-manual instances have no symlinks to repair.
A yellow or red banner at the top of the main menu means claude-multi found problems. Press ! to open the health screen. Select an issue to see its detail and suggested fix.

head: Problem
Cause
Fix
rows: Instance directory was deleted outside claude-multi
Remove the instance or recreate the directory
Wrapper script was deleted or its directory moved
Wrapper points at an old Claude Code install
Fix the JSON or restore a copy from ~/.claude-multi/backups/ if one exists
Plugin or skill links point at missing targets
A config schema migration was interrupted
Restore the newest backup and retry
Instance settings are behind the current version

blocks.html: Some terminals, including older SSH clients, do not handle the Ink-based React TUI well.
Force the simpler prompts-based UI:
The flows are the same. Only the rendering changes.
If Claude Code cannot authenticate with your provider:

items.html: Check the instance fields with claude-multi info <name>. The provider and region should match the account you are using.
Check the base URL. MiMo and Qwen have separate templates for pay-per-token and subscription plans, and the wrong template points at the wrong endpoint.

blocks.html: The file path is ~/.claude-<name>/settings.json, not ~/.claude-multi/<name>/settings.json.

If the key is stored under ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN and the endpoint matches your plan, test the key with the provider’s own API before changing claude-multi. A 401 from the provider means the key or account is the problem, not the wrapper.
Some providers use different base URLs for pay-per-token and subscription plans:
If you are on a subscription plan but used the pay-per-token template, or the other way around, the API key will not authenticate. Remove the instance and recreate it with the correct template.
For mimo-token, also check the region. cn, sgp, and ams use different hostnames, so create the instance with the region your subscription was issued for.
Instance names must be unique. Pick a different name or remove the existing one first:

blocks.code:
claude-multi remove deepseek
claude-multi add deepseek --provider deepseek --api-key sk-...

blocks.html: remove leaves the old config directory in place. If you recreate the instance with the same name, it reuses ~/.claude-deepseek/, so delete that directory first if you want a clean start.
If an MCP server fails to connect:

items.html: Check the config shape with claude-multi mcp verify <instance>. A stdio entry needs a command; an HTTP or SSE entry needs a url.
Check for name collisions with claude-multi plugins check-collisions <instance> <plugin-id>.
Start the instance and run /mcp to see whether the server connected and which tools it exposes.

blocks.html: mcp verify reads the config only. It does not start the server or test the port. If the command path is wrong or the server crashes on startup, /mcp and the server’s own logs are the places to look.
If a config schema migration was interrupted:

items.html: Check migrationMeta.migrationStatus in ~/.claude-multi/config.json. A failed migration also records failureInfo with the failed step and error.
Look in ~/.claude-multi/backups/. Each backup is a timestamped directory containing config.json and the instance settings.json files.
Restore the newest backup over the current files if the config is unusable, then run claude-multi doctor check. Loading the restored config retries the migration.
Press ! in the TUI to open the health screen and read the failure detail. Press r there to re-run the health checks.

blocks.html: claude-multi keeps the newest three backup directories. A migration takes a PID lock, so a stale lock older than 30 minutes is removed automatically.
After upgrading claude-multi, run:

blocks.code:
claude-multi doctor check
claude-multi doctor fix

blocks.html: doctor check reports instances created by an older version and provider settings that differ from the current template. doctor fix rewrites stale wrappers, then asks whether to run the pending instance migrations. A migration backs up the config and settings before it changes anything. It leaves your API keys and custom tuning values alone, except for documented legacy defaults.

If both commands report nothing, the template itself has not changed in that release. Check the provider pages for manual model overrides when a vendor retires a model before claude-multi ships a template update.
Update checks are opt-in. Enable them:
Or check Claude Code manually:
To check the claude-multi version, run claude-multi --version.

items.html: Run claude-multi list to see every instance, its paths, and its sync mode
Run claude-multi doctor check for a health report with suggested fixes
Check the GitHub issues for known problems
Open a new issue with your claude-multi --version output and the contents of ~/.claude-multi/config.json
